Whether the lock is removed in every case depends on evals/run.py, which is not in this packet.

terms.meaning: a script that Git runs just before saving a commit, and which can stop that commit
a small file that signals a process is busy, so other steps wait until it is removed
a deliberate small defect put into code on purpose, to check that the tests catch it
the number a program returns when it finishes, where zero means success and any other number means failure

used_by: evals/run.py creates the lock file it reads

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and where the lock lives
sections.what: Explains that this check blocks commits while the mutation runner has a source file deliberately broken. It also fixes where the lock file is expected.
sections.why: The docstring explains that a commit during that window would make the defect the stored source.
sections.watch_out: The lock file name must match exactly what the mutation runner creates.

sections.name: refusal
sections.title: Build the refusal message
sections.what: Returns the refusal text when the lock exists, naming the entry in flight and what to do, and returns an empty text when there is no lock.
sections.why: The message tells the reader that waiting for the run is the fix.
sections.watch_out: An empty lock file produces the text an unnamed entry, which is the only fallback.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Check the lock and set the result
sections.what: Reads an optional path, checks for a refusal, prints it to the error output if one exists, and returns status 1 to stop the commit.
sections.why: Git stops a commit when the hook returns a non-zero status.
sections.watch_out: A path argument replaces the default lock location, so a wrong argument silently checks the wrong place.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Script start
sections.what: Runs the check when the file is run directly, and passes its result on as the exit status.
sections.why: Standard pattern for a runnable Python script.

summary: A commit check that refuses a commit while the mutation runner has a source file deliberately broken.
purpose: Stops a deliberately defective file from being saved into the repository. The mutation runner in evals/run.py patches a tracked file, runs tests, then restores it. This check blocks commits during that window.
why: The file's docstring says that detecting a changed file is not enough, because a race can be lost silently. A lock file held for the run is the simpler guarantee.
how: 1. The mutation runner creates a lock file named .mutation-in-flight at the repository root. 2. Git runs the pre-commit hook, which calls this script. 3. The script checks whether the lock exists. 4. If it exists, the script reads the entry name and prints a refusal message. 5. The script returns status 1, which stops the commit. If the lock is absent, it returns status 0.
inputs: An optional path to a lock file given on the command line. Without one, the default lock at the repository root is used.
outputs: A refusal message on the error output and exit status 1 when a run is in flight. Otherwise, exit status 0 and no output.
risks: If the lock is left behind after a crash, every commit is refused until someone removes it. A wrong path argument checks the wrong file and can let a commit through.
debug: If commits are refused with no run active, check the lock file's contents and that no run is still going. The refusal message gives the next steps. If a commit gets through during a run, check that the hook is installed through the hooks path setting described in the docstring.
